## System

| | |
|---|---|
| **Machine** | Acer Predator Helios Neo 16 (PHN16-72): i5-14500HX, 16 GB RAM |
| **OS** | Arch Linux |
| **Kernel** | linux-cachyos-bore 7.3.5 (BORE scheduler) |
| **Bootloader** | Limine: Arch Linux (CachyOS kernel), Windows and the latest snapshot |
| **Boot splash** | Plymouth with my own logo |
| **Disk** | btrfs on LUKS; snapper + snap-pac take a snapshot on every pacman run |
| **Swap** | zram, plus a swapfile for hibernation |
| **Packages** | pacman, yay for the AUR, Flatpak; kernel from `[cachyos-v3]` |
| **Graphics** | Intel drives the laptop screen, NVIDIA RTX 4060 on nvidia-open |
| **Audio** | PipeWire + WirePlumber |
| **Network** | NetworkManager, ufw firewall |
| **Power** | power-profiles-daemon, thermald, intel-lpmd |

Configs:

- [`/etc/boot/hooks/pre.d/20-skyylimine-snapshots-section`](root/etc/boot/hooks/pre.d/20-skyylimine-snapshots-section): Limine hook: hands the tools a /Snapshots section before they run
- [`/etc/boot/hooks/post.d/40-skyylimine-menu-layout`](root/etc/boot/hooks/post.d/40-skyylimine-menu-layout): Limine hook: OS > Arch Linux / Windows menu, drops "EFI fallback"
- [`/etc/boot/hooks/post.d/50-skyylimine-snapshot-latest`](root/etc/boot/hooks/post.d/50-skyylimine-snapshot-latest): Limine hook: one "snapshot-latest" boot entry
- [`/etc/boot/hooks/post.d/60-skyylimine-snapshot-in-os`](root/etc/boot/hooks/post.d/60-skyylimine-snapshot-in-os): Limine hook: puts snapshot-latest last in OS, no Snapshots header
- [`/etc/default/limine`](root/etc/default/limine): Limine settings: boot order, snapshot entries
- [`~/.config/limine`](home/.config/limine): Limine theme: header.conf and the wallpaper generator
- [`/etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d/zz-hybrid-gpu.conf`](root/etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d/zz-hybrid-gpu.conf): Keep nouveau + its firmware out of the kernel images
- [`/etc/pacman.d/mirrorlist.arch`](root/etc/pacman.d/mirrorlist.arch): Spare copy of the ranked Arch mirrorlist

## Fonts

| | |
|---|---|
| **CozetteVector** | everywhere: bar, terminal, login screen, Pear Desktop and Beeper. `yay -S cozette-ttf` |
| **Nerd Fonts Symbols** | icons in the bar and terminal. `sudo pacman -S ttf-nerd-fonts-symbols` |
| **Noto** | fallback for every script, CJK and colour emoji. `sudo pacman -S noto-fonts noto-fonts-cjk noto-fonts-emoji` |
| **Liberation** | the default sans and serif. `sudo pacman -S ttf-liberation` |
| **iA Writer** | iA Writer Mono, Duo and Quattro. `yay -S ttf-ia-writer` |
| **Font Awesome** | Font Awesome icons. `sudo pacman -S woff2-font-awesome` |
| **Zpix** | pixel font with Chinese and Japanese (skyydb uses it, and Pear, Beeper and Vesktop fall back to it): `zpix.ttf` from the [Zpix releases](https://github.com/SolidZORO/zpix-pixel-font/releases/latest) into `~/.local/share/fonts/zpix/`, then `fc-cache -f` |
| **RuneScape** | Plain 11, Plain 12, Bold 12, Quill, Quill 8 (Vesktop's font), Quill Caps, Barbarian Assault: from `RuneScape-Fonts.zip` in the [RuneStar fonts releases](https://github.com/RuneStar/fonts/releases/latest), the `ttf/` files except Fairy and Surok, into `~/.local/share/fonts/runescape/`, then `fc-cache -f` |
| **fuck-omarchy icons** | the fork's own icon font: installed with fuck-omarchy into `~/.local/share/fonts/fuck-omarchy/` |

## Restore on a new machine

`home/` mirrors `~` and `root/` mirrors `/`, so `home/.config/hypr` goes back to `~/.config/hypr`.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/l4n1skyy/dotfiles.git ~/Shared/03_AREAS/_DOTFILES
rsync -av ~/Shared/03_AREAS/_DOTFILES/home/ ~/                      # put the configs back
sudo pacman -S --needed - < ~/Shared/03_AREAS/_DOTFILES/packages/pacman.txt
yay -S --needed - < ~/Shared/03_AREAS/_DOTFILES/packages/aur.txt
```

Secrets were replaced with `<redacted>` in `home/.bashrc`; fill those in by hand.

Not copied because they match fuck-omarchy's defaults: `.config/autostart`, `.config/starship.toml`.

## Updating

```bash
dotfiles              # copy current configs here and rebuild this README
dotfiles -n           # preview what would change
dotfiles --push       # same as `dotfiles`, then commit and push to GitHub
dotfiles -p -m "msg"  # push with your own commit message
dotfiles --edit       # edit dotfiles.conf
```

The script lives at `~/.local/bin/system/dotfiles` (copied here under `home/.local/bin/system/`).
